problem_text:
A logistics coordinator is tasked with allocating a set of critical components into standardized transport modules. The components are as follows:

* Component Alpha: mass 34 units
* Component Beta: mass 34 units
* Component Gamma: mass 35 units
* Component Delta: mass 44 units
* Component Epsilon: mass 67 units
* Component Zeta: mass 69 units
* Component Eta: mass 32 units
* Component Theta: mass 70 units
* Component Iota: mass 50 units
* Component Kappa: mass 51 units
* Component Lambda: mass 68 units
* Component Mu: mass 68 units
* Component Nu: mass 59 units
* Component Xi: mass 31 units
* Component Omicron: mass 64 units
* Component Pi: mass 68 units
* Component Rho: mass 61 units
* Component Sigma: mass 55 units
* Component Tau: mass 48 units
* Component Upsilon: mass 69 units
* Component Phi: mass 31 units
* Component Chi: mass 45 units
* Component Psi: mass 52 units
* Component Omega: mass 52 units
* Component Aleph: mass 50 units
* Component Beth: mass 40 units
* Component Gimel: mass 56 units
* Component Dalet: mass 42 units
* Component He: mass 55 units
* Component Waw: mass 33 units
* Component Zayin: mass 31 units
* Component Het: mass 47 units
* Component Tet: mass 68 units
* Component Yod: mass 64 units
* Component Kaf: mass 43 units
* Component Lamed: mass 49 units
* Component Mem: mass 39 units
* Component Nun: mass 68 units

Each transport module possesses a maximum safe load capacity of 100 mass units. The coordinator must devise an allocation scheme that places every component into precisely one module, ensuring the aggregate mass within any single module does not surpass the stipulated limit. The paramount objective is to accomplish this distribution utilizing the minimal possible number of modules.
